title: Prism: a model that remembers
description: Grow a language model and keep a record of every change. Prism is a .NET decode gate and lineage journal, and the code behind the Prism chat tool.

sizzle.headline: A model that remembers how it grew.
sizzle.sub: Prism picks each next word by how confident the model is, records every time you grow the model, and works out how it stood at any past round. It is the code behind the Prism chat in your browser.

stats.label: checks that the decode gate matches the hand-written code it replaced, with zero mismatches
to open a journal of 50,000 events, far more than a real model records

items.text: The gate was compared with the decode code in the app that trains the Prism model, over 30,400 checks, and every one agreed. That app now routes its decoding through the package.

items.claim: A journal that opens in 19.5 ms at 50,000 events
items.text: Measured once on a synthetic worst case: 50,000 hand-built events in an in-memory store, with each derivation then taking 2 to 15 ms. A real model's journal holds one line per growth or setting change, typically tens.

build.title: What you can build
build.line: Each one is in the package today.

items.title: Decoding that knows when to guess
items.text: Commit greedily when the model is confident, otherwise sample only from what clears the floor. One tested policy, with a resonance floor, no floor, or nucleus sampling.

items.title: Growth with a receipt
items.text: Grow a model's context, layers, shifts or vocabulary, and the journal is stamped for you. A model cannot grow without the record.

items.title: Answers about the past that stay true
items.text: How ramped is this layer? When did the model last grow? Each is answered from the history stamped at the time, never from whatever a constant holds today.

items.title: A guard against collapse
items.text: DegenGuard fires on a run of repeated tokens or a run of non-greedy picks, the two signs that decoding has collapsed.

items.title: A journal that runs in a browser tab
items.text: A file-backed store for servers and a pure in-memory store for browser hosts that have no file system.

intro: Prism is the NuGet package that the Prism chat tool runs on. It holds three things for a model built on AlgFormer: the decode policy that chooses each next token, a lineage journal that records how the model grew, and a growth surface that changes the model and writes that record for you.

why.title: One decode policy
why.text: Commit greedily when the model is confident, otherwise sample only from what clears the floor. The gate is one tested policy with an explicit floor mode: a resonance floor for the holographic core, no floor, or nucleus sampling.

why.title: Facts about the past stay facts
why.text: Every structural change is stamped with the parameters a later calculation needs, when it happens. Questions such as how ramped a layer is, or when the model last grew, are answered from that history and never from whatever a live constant holds today.

why.title: Growth that records itself
why.text: Growing context, layers, shifts or vocabulary through the growth surface stamps the journal automatically, so a model cannot grow without the record.

capabilities.title: Lineage journal
capabilities.text: Idempotent append, so a resumed process stamping the same event again is a no-op. Derivations AlphaAt, DepthAt, LastGrowthRound and AddRoundOf resolve against the stamped history, including layers inserted at the front.

capabilities.title: Storage seam
capabilities.text: A file-backed JSONL store with durable append, and a pure in-memory store for browser and WebAssembly hosts that have no file system.

capabilities.title: Growth surface
capabilities.text: Grow a HoloFormer's context, layers, shifts or vocabulary, correct by construction, with the lineage stamped for you.

capabilities.title: Decode policy and gate
capabilities.text: DecodePolicy, Gate and GateDecision implement the confidence-gated decode with an explicit FloorMode.

capabilities.title: Degeneration guard
capabilities.text: DegenGuard fires on a run of repeated tokens or a run of non-greedy picks, the two signs that decoding has collapsed.
